### Observed differences

- Six activities — A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 — each ran in about 48–52 in 100 traces in the earlier window and in about 98–100 in 100 in the later window, exactly once per trace in both windows (no repetitions). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the earlier window these six formed two mutually exclusive trios: A28, A30 and A31 always ran together (about 49 in 100 traces), A32, A33 and A34 always ran together (about 51 in 100), and a cross-trio pair such as A28 with A32 never shared a trace. In the later window, cross-trio pairs co-occur in about 98 in 100 traces. [REL013, REL025, REL015, REL019, REL022, REL024]
- In the later window the trios also run in a fixed sequence: every first-trio activity precedes every second-trio activity in about 98 in 100 traces (for example A30 before A32), while the order inside each trio stays unfixed (A28 before A30 in about 49 in 100 later traces, A30 before A28 in about 50 in 100). [REL019, REL013, REL018, REL027]
- The surrounding frame is unchanged: A25 still precedes the whole segment (A25 before A28 observable in about 99 in 100 later traces, up from about 49 in 100, simply because A28 now always runs), and the first trio still precedes A26 (A28 before A26 in about 99 in 100 later traces). [REL001, REL004, REL007, REL010]
- The segment grew by about three positions: the gap from A25 to A34 moved from 1–3 steps (essentially all earlier pair observations) to 4–5 steps (about 98 in 100 later), and A31 to A26 likewise from 1–3 to 4–5 steps; relative positions shifted consistently — A25 earlier (mean 0.67 to 0.62), A26 later (0.80 to 0.83), the first trio earlier (about 0.74 to 0.68) and the second trio later (about 0.73 to 0.77). [LAG003, LAG006, LAG001, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS008]
- Successors were redistributed: A25's observed outgoing transitions moved from a fairly even spread over all six activities (14–19% each) to a concentration on A30, A28 and A31 (about 30–38% each), with A32 and A34 below 2% and A33 unobserved; A28, A30 and A31 now rarely lead directly to A26 (that share fell from about 30–36% to under 1% or to unobserved). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A25 and A26 changed from an exclusive choice to a full sequence: in the earlier window each case executed either the trio A28–A30–A31 (about 49 in 100 cases) or the trio A32–A33–A34 (about 51 in 100), never both, whereas in the later window both trios run in about 98–100 in 100 cases — first A28/A30/A31, then A32/A33/A34, with no fixed order inside each trio and A25 and A26 still bracketing the segment. [REL015, REL019, REL013, REL025, OCC001, OCC004]

The support is direct and consistent: the relational items show the change itself (cross-trio co-occurrence from 0 to about 98 in 100, fixed first-to-second order, A25 now leading into the first trio and the first trio rarely into A26), the participation items show all six activities becoming near-mandatory, and the distance, position and successor items all match one trios-inserted-before-the-other reading. The 51 qualifying items are many times the roughly 0.59 expected by chance among the 118 tested units, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits, so sampling variation cannot explain the pattern as a whole (representative items [OCC001, REL015, LAG003, DIR001]). An important competing explanation remains: from these window-level aggregates one cannot tell whether the earlier either-or pattern was a per-case routing choice or a mixture of two case variants; also, direction shares cover only observed transitions, so an unobserved edge such as A25 to A33 in the later window is not proof that the edge was removed.

Other differences: none — every qualifying item concerns these six activities and their relations with A25 and A26. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL001, REL015, LAG003, DIR001]
